name: Rowan Kamara-Park
role: Retired union leader, former Dearborn Forge machine workers' organizer
location: Avalon Quiet, the Foundry Rest, Unit 9 (a former union hall converted to senior housing), near Lincoln and Addison
description:
Rowan Kamara-Park is a person of considerable physical presence despite their age — still broad through the shoulders, hands that are visibly enlarged by decades of machine work and two decades of chrome reinforcement, skin the color of dark river clay mapped with old hydraulic burns along both forearms. They have a full beard, silver-white, kept long and braided with small steel hex-nuts — not decoration but notation: each nut represents a contract won. There are thirty-one of them. Their eyes are deep-set under heavy brows and have been modified with retinal overlays that display scrolling text when they are reading union documents, which is often. They move slowly but without any suggestion that the slowness is weakness.

Rowan Kamara-Park organized workers at Dearborn Forge for forty-one years, starting as a floor welder and ending as the most recognizable union figure in GLMZ's manufacturing sector. They retired at seventy-eight when their heart required a significant reconstruction, and they have spent the five years since refusing to actually retire in any functional sense — still advising, still reviewing contracts, still showing up to shop-floor solidarity actions in a mobility assist suit they make no attempt to hide. They are living legend to people who know the labor history and an incomprehensible relic to people who don't, and they genuinely do not care which category any given person falls into. They are here and they are working.

core_fears: That the institutional memory of the union will be lost when their generation is gone — that workers fifty years from now will fight the same fights from scratch
That the MMWA's current leadership will make a concession that undermines something it took decades to win
core_desires: A documented legacy — not for their own sake but so future workers have the map
To see one more genuinely transformative contract before they die
coping_mechanisms: Converts everything into a project — grief, frustration, fear — there is always a next step
Physical ritual: they polish the hex-nuts in their beard every evening, reviewing the memory attached to each one
blind_spots: Can be impatient with hesitation in ways that intimidate younger organizers into silence — they have fought too many fights to easily remember how it felt not to know how to fight
Tends to see every situation through a labor-capital frame, which is often correct and occasionally misses what's actually happening
psychology.secret: In 2178, during a critical contract negotiation that Miroljub is credited with winning, they accepted a private meeting with a Ringo Corporation intermediary who offered to weaken a competitor's position in exchange for a specific carve-out in the MMWA's medical coverage terms. Miroljub refused the carve-out but did not report the approach — and used the intelligence the intermediary accidentally revealed about the competitor to win the contract. The win was real. The method had a shadow in it that they have never discussed.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Floor-worker vernacular mixed with the formal register of contract language — they can shift between them in a single sentence; uses collective pronouns instinctively ('we fought for this'; 'they took that from us'); Serbian-Ghanaian cadences in the rhythm of long sentences
speech_patterns.cadence: Builds slowly and then arrives with full weight; they are not hurrying for anyone
verbal_tics: 'You understand what I'm telling you' after making a point they consider essential
'We called it—' before any piece of labor history jargon they need to define for younger people
A short dry laugh before disagreeing with someone they respect
example_lines: 'In 2178 we had thirty-seven people out for nineteen days. Ringo thought we'd break at fourteen. We understood something they did not: a worker who has held the line once is not the same worker anymore. You understand what I'm telling you.'

'The pension legislation they're proposing has a clause on page forty-one — we called it a horizon clause, because it moves forward every year so you never quite reach it. I wrote a memo about horizon clauses in 2169. I will find you a copy.'

story_hooks: A current MMWA contract negotiation contains a buried clause that Miroljub recognizes from 2178 — the same Ringo intermediary structure that approached them then — and they need someone to trace the current players without exposing their own history with it

A box of union archives from the 2160s-2180s has been discovered in the Foundry Rest's basement, sealed and water-damaged; Miroljub believes they contain documentation of corporate violations that were covered up at the time and are relevant to a current case

A young worker at Dearborn Forge has been quietly organizing and has made a tactical error that is about to get them fired — Miroljub needs someone to intervene in a way that cannot be traced back to union leadership
narrative_function: Labor history resource and moral authority figure; can provide context on manufacturing sector politics, corporate-union conflicts, and the history of working conditions at every major Meridian facility. Quest giver for labor-related plots; also a portrait of what it looks like to build collective power in a corporate city.
augmentations: Chrome-reinforced hand and forearm skeletal structure (bilateral, industrial-grade, installed 2163 as workplace accommodation); cardiac reconstruction mesh (installed 2195, heart failure); retinal overlay implants (both eyes, union contract review overlay, installed 2171); mobility assist exo-suit (external, worn daily, configured to look like clothing when possible)
daily_life: Rises late, reads labor news and pension legislation for two hours, then takes calls and visits from current union members seeking advice. They attend every MMWA meeting they can reach regardless of weather or difficulty and have been known to appear at shop-floor actions by mobility-suited transit when younger organizers told them it was not necessary. They maintain a shrine to the ELF they believe inhabits the Foundry Rest's building systems — an old machine union ELF they call Strojna, leaving it small machine components as offerings.
affiliation: Meridian Manufacturing Workers' Alliance (MMWA) — emeritus; Dearborn Forge Retirees Collective; loosely, the Avalon Quiet community council

decision_rules: The collective interest takes precedence over any individual interest, including their own — this is not abstract, they have applied it to themselves at cost
Never burn a relationship permanently if there is any chance it can be rebuilt usefully later
escalation_ladder: Listens completely — they are assessing not just what is said but what isn't
Asks the question that reframes the situation
States their analysis directly and proposes action
Mobilizes whatever network or resource is appropriate
In extremis, becomes entirely focused and operates with a speed and clarity that surprises people who only know the deliberate elder

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Assessing; gives them a chance to demonstrate what they are; not warm but not hostile — waiting to see
interpersonal_modes.friends: Direct, warm, demanding in the sense that they expect you to be as serious as they are and are delighted when you are

stress_responses.low: Polishes the hex-nuts; reviews contract language; makes calls
stress_responses.medium: Becomes very still; thinking through contingencies; stops speaking unless they have something specific to say
stress_responses.high: Activates — becomes more energized, not less; this is what they were built for

contradictions: Believes in transparency and collective decision-making as fundamental values — and has once made a unilateral decision in shadow that shaped a decade of union history, and has protected that shadow ever since
habits: Polishes the hex-nuts in their beard every evening and names each contract aloud quietly
Leaves a machine component — a small gear or bolt — at the Strojna shrine every morning
Reads every contract they are given, fully, regardless of length
breaking_points: Watching a contract they won being signed away in a concession they were not consulted on
Someone using the 2178 situation to discredit the union rather than Miroljub personally — they will take the damage to themselves but not to the institution

cyberware_inventory.condition: aging but functional; occasional joint resistance in cold
well-maintained; configured for low profile under clothing

timeline.event: Born in Dearborn Forge district to a Serbian-Montenegrin father and Ghanaian-Fijian mother
Hired as floor welder at Dearborn Forge
Joins the nascent MMWA; becomes a shop steward within two years
Chrome hand/forearm reinforcement installed following industrial injury
Elected to MMWA leadership; retinal overlays installed for contract work
The Ringo approach and the contract victory; thirty-seven workers, nineteen days
Heart failure; cardiac reconstruction; first genuine period of reduced activity
Formally steps back from MMWA leadership but begins informal advisory role that is functionally equivalent

physical_description.heritage: Sub-Saharan African (37.1%), East Asian (32.1%), Indigenous American (23.6%), and Hispanic/Latin American (7.2%) ancestry creates a distinctive phenotype: Sub-Saharan African foundation provides facial fullness, lip definition, and warm undertone base; East Asian ancestry contributes prominent cheekbones, eye shape epicanthic fold tendency, and structural geometry; Indigenous American heritage adds warm terracotta and amber skin depth; Hispanic/Latin American admixture enhances warm golden undertones throughout. The result is a unified warm-brown complexion with mahogany-to-copper richness rather than equal-measure blend.
physical_description.build: Broad-shouldered and thick-chested despite age; considerable mass concentrated in torso and upper body from five decades of welding and machine work. Legs slightly atrophied from reliance on mobility assist, but arms remain visibly muscular beneath loose skin.
physical_description.hair_style: Full, braided beard with thirty-one small steel hex-nuts woven throughout; each nut represents a won contract from their organizing years
physical_description.eye_color: Deep brown, modified with subtle retinal overlay implants that display scrolling text during reading
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm deep brown with mahogany-to-aged-copper richness; dominant Sub-Saharan warmth layered with East Asian undertone clarity and Indigenous American terracotta-amber depth. Significant weathering visible across face and neck from five decades of industrial work and age.
physical_description.complexion: Blended facial structure: Sub-Saharan African fullness in lips and cheek prominence combined with East Asian high cheekbone definition and characteristic eye shape; Indigenous American warmth throughout complexion creating golden-amber undertones in skin. Deep-set eyes beneath pronounced brows; face bears character of decades of shop-floor work. Hydraulic burns visible along both forearms as darker, scarred patches. Hands visibly enlarged from machine work and chrome reinforcement.
distinguishing_marks: Bilateral hydraulic burns running in streaked patterns along both forearms from mid-wrist to elbow, darker and raised against surrounding skin
Chromatic scarring where hand/forearm chrome skeletal reinforcement meets natural tissue at wrists and elbows
Deep calloused ridges across palms and along all finger joints, visible even in old age
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Chrome-reinforced hands and forearms (industrial-grade, visible at wrists as smooth metallic caps and along forearm musculature as subtle chrome striating); external mobility assist exo-suit worn daily (configured to resemble heavy tactical clothing, gunmetal gray and worn matte black, fitted over shoulders and spine); retinal implants barely visible as slight amber luminescence in deep-set eyes when active
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves deliberately and without hurry; the slowness is intentional and carries weight rather than frailty. Stands with a slight forward lean supported by the exo-suit. Hands often remain in lap or folded across chest when seated. Makes direct eye contact without apology. Voice is steady but deepened by age and cardiac reconstruction.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3 working-class aesthetic, deliberately maintained as such despite pension stability. Favors worn denim work shirts (often union-logoed), heavy canvas pants, and sturdy boots suitable for shop floors. Exo-suit worn visibly over clothing rather than concealed. A battered union pin from 2154 is always affixed to collar. Wears a simple steel wedding band and a copper wire bracelet twisted by hand (claimed to communicate with building ELF systems, though likely symbolic).
